bug_semantics: HTTPEndpoint derived an attribute name directly from the client-controlled HTTP method and invoked that attribute through getattr. When Route was configured without an explicit methods list, a non-standard method such as _DO_DELETE could therefore select an internal endpoint helper named _do_delete and bypass authorization or other checks enforced by the intended public handler.
flaw_origin: PR #52 introduced class-based HTTP views. Its first reconstructable member commit dd11c69b5b115bc97b7139c59fbd1dd555c4fbde added starlette/views.py and implemented View.dispatch with getattr(self, request_method.lower(), None), making an unvalidated HTTP method an attribute selector. The member's immediate parent had no starlette/views.py, so this is the smallest public commit that first wrote the vulnerable mechanism; the later mainline squash 0693a8f6c982eb01e6b1b41ac4e5b74f67140301 merely landed the PR's final tree.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object dd11c69b5b115bc97b7139c59fbd1dd555c4fbde names human author and committer erm <jermff@gmail.com>; its message is 'Renaming asgi_application, implementing CBV pattern, add_route method on router' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot marker.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-x746-7m8f-x49c and CVE.org CVE-2026-48817 describe the same unsafe-reflection path: an unconstrained Route lets a non-standard request method reach HTTPEndpoint, whose lowercased method name selected and invoked an unintended attribute; CVE.org state is PUBLISHED, not rejected or withdrawn.

GitHub PR #52 commit API enumerates eight member commits. The first, dd11c69b5b115bc97b7139c59fbd1dd555c4fbde, adds starlette/views.py and its patch contains request_method = request.method (HEAD mapped to GET), followed by func = getattr(self, request_method.lower(), None) and func(request).

Direct parent-tree verification: dd11c69b5b115bc97b7139c59fbd1dd555c4fbde has parent 945543aeaf4784b78607350c25b36aac01dcdbfd, and GitHub's contents endpoint for starlette/views.py at that parent returns HTTP 404; the vulnerable class and dispatch code are absent.

Squash decomposition: PR #52 head d03e8baec0e1684971e6d377af45bb861bd025cc and landed mainline squash 0693a8f6c982eb01e6b1b41ac4e5b74f67140301 both have tree 65e8c51cbeaa889a411add19538f48c703fd97e3, while the squash commit message lists the reconstructed member subjects.

Local full-history git -S and --follow inspection traces the unsafe getattr dispatch through the starlette/views.py to starlette/endpoints.py rename; f4fe0ec312e30e50f7b37cf6d359700630d0d2be is a 91%-similar rename and not the BIC.

BIC commit-object inspection shows author erm <jermff@gmail.com>, committer erm <jermff@gmail.com>, and no trailers or AI/bot marker; AI attribution is therefore absent on the atomic introducer itself.

Atomic fix member c76a277005e7674ee92c35690fc00be3b299f594 changes starlette/endpoints.py so dispatch calls getattr only when request.method is in self._allowed_methods (with the explicit HEAD/GET exception), otherwise selecting method_not_allowed; its regression test sends _DO_DELETE and requires HTTP 405.

Mainline fix e3f972225adb1d84b80dba132f520cc24cb84229 applies the same endpoint guard and regression test over parent 348f86dc92fed6e3c0314154e38deec90a6bcabd; git shows it is absent from tag 1.0.0 and is an ancestor of tag 1.1.0.

Release topology matches the advisory: the landed vulnerable PR is contained from tag 0.2.1 onward, tag 1.0.0 still contains the unrestricted getattr dispatch, tag 1.1.0 resolves to a4ff83b1aacaf8955e241dd00444c27823be163a and contains e3f972225adb1d84b80dba132f520cc24cb84229, matching first_patched_version 1.1.0.
reasoning: The advisory is a real published vulnerability, not a false positive. The externally supplied method token crossed Route without a method allowlist and became an object-attribute selector inside HTTPEndpoint.dispatch, so an endpoint helper with a matching lowercase name could be invoked as a handler. Mainline history initially points to squash 0693a8f6c982eb01e6b1b41ac4e5b74f67140301, but PR #52's retained member chain is reconstructable and proves that dd11c69b5b115bc97b7139c59fbd1dd555c4fbde first added the unsafe dispatch; its immediate parent lacks the file entirely. Later refactors and the views-to-endpoints rename preserve rather than introduce the mechanism. PR #3286's atomic member c76a277005e7674ee92c35690fc00be3b299f594 directly fixes it by restricting dispatch to declared standard verbs, and mainline e3f972225adb1d84b80dba132f520cc24cb84229 carries that fix into 1.1.0 while 1.0.0 remains vulnerable. The atomic BIC's own commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
